summary: The prepared source already contains the issue-relevant ordinary CPU weight-loading correction from upstream PR 34064: compatible unquantized TP=1 checkpoint tensors are adopted as parameter storage, avoiding a second full tensor allocation/copy per pure-SP rank. Current regressions and independent CPU/GPU storage boundaries pass; the exact four-GPU Qwen-Image OOM was not reproducible with the available hardware and weights.

tests.what_was_measured: 18 loader tests passed, including CPU checkpoint-storage pointer adoption, numerical equality, unsupported-layout rejection, rank-local loading boundaries, and real GPU copy/adoption behavior.
Three independent storage boundaries passed: CPU TP=1 zero-copy adoption, ordinary GPU copy semantics, and direct GPU zero-copy adoption; all validate tensor numerics.
5 host-spill tests passed for file-backed fused tensors, sealed reuse, disk-space fallback, and checkpoint identity. This is supporting loader coverage, not evidence for discrete-GPU applicability.

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 executed the two CUDA-API GPU storage-boundary tests under PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; both passed and were not skipped.

remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 GPU was assigned; the reported four-rank SP=4 topology was unavailable.
Qwen/Qwen-Image weights were unavailable, so the actual 38 GiB DiT and HTTP serving path were not run.
The source report used four NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada GPUs and CUDA; NVIDIA-specific behavior was not validated on the AMD GPU.
No end-to-end image semantic or distributed correctness claim is made.
Upstream PR 34064 provides a Qwen-Image startup benchmark for the relevant corrected path, but this investigation did not independently repeat that full-model benchmark.
